items.description: Opt-in external activity telemetry, disabled by default. Sources require explicit authorization. Enabling this does not enable runtime connections, change agent presence or grant permissions.

Maximum validity in seconds for new external activity reports; default 3600. Omitted report TTL is fixed at 90 seconds by the protocol. A lower maximum requires an explicit smaller TTL on new reports; accepted replays retain their original expiry.
Allowed future clock skew in seconds for a new external report; default 30. Skew never extends validity beyond the report TTL from Server receipt.
Seconds without a current source report before external source activity is stale; default 30. This does not change agent presence, sessions or execution capacity.
Maximum admitted external reports per minute for one source; default 60.
Maximum accumulated report burst for one external source; default 20.
Maximum admitted external reports per minute across one agent's sources; default 1920.
Maximum accumulated report burst across one agent's external sources; default 80.
Maximum admitted external reports per minute across this installation; default 8192.
Maximum accumulated external report burst across this installation; default 512.
Maximum registered external observation sources for one agent; default 32.
Maximum registered external observation sources in this installation; default 4096.
Maximum registered external observed instances in this installation; default 4096.

Maximum external correlation records in this installation, including retained cleared/revoked records; default 4096. Clearing does not free a record. Lowering the limit preserves existing records and permits their updates.
Maximum active publish credentials for one observation source; default 8.
External observation event history retention in days; default 7. Replay and generation fences are preserved separately.
Maximum retained external observation events; default 20000. This does not cap canonical coordination history.

When another registered Connector machine requests the same agent: require approval (default), deny, or accept and revoke the previous machine. Automatic replacement preserves approved harness settings and the remaining execution budget and expiry; the first machine always needs approval.

When a runtime agent is busy and a sender queues a newer message, off (default) delivers every message as its own turn. same_sender cancels the sender's earlier unsent messages with the same session affinity and adds their text to the newer turn. A message that reached the runtime is never cancelled.

Allow HTTP/HTTPS and WS/WSS (default), or require HTTPS/WSS. Configure TLS before selecting HTTPS only. Applies to new requests and connections; restart to close existing streams. TLS can terminate at a trusted reverse proxy.

When a runtime installation updates to a newer build: 'review' (default) holds the new build for operator review. 'follow' adopts one strictly newer build under the approved installation and keeps live sessions.
New connection key lifetime in seconds; 86400 = 24 hours, 0 = unlimited. Agents may override this default. Existing keys keep their issued expiry.
Seconds without a heartbeat before an active session shows as 'stale' (amber on the graph). Too short causes false alarms; too long hides stuck agents.
Presence window (s): with a heartbeat older than this the agent drops out of the broadcast audience and shows offline on the dashboard.
Heartbeat age (s) past which abandoned sessions are closed automatically (opportunistic reaper).
Lease (s) of a claimed handoff: without completion within it, the claim expires and the work returns to the pool for another agent.
Tell the creator and the previous claimant when a handoff lease expires. Both notices start a turn when the agent has a runtime session.
Fraction of the handoff lease after which the creator gets one warning when the claimant sent no message to the creator. 0 turns the warning off.
Maximum relay depth of one chain. A relay past this depth is refused. Applies to new chains only.
Maximum executions that one root message can start. Applies to new roots only.
Seconds that a root message chain can run before it closes. Applies to new roots only.
Lease (s) for messages pulled via inbox_pull: without an ack within it, the delivery returns to 'unread'.
Ceiling (s) for the timeout parameter of message_wait/event_wait (agent long polling).
Internal interval (ms) between checks in long-polling waits. Lower = more responsive, more SQLite read load.
PRAGMA busy_timeout (ms): how long a connection waits for SQLite locks before failing. Affects new connections.
Maximum events returned per page in event_get/event_wait and the dashboard feed.
TTL (s) for ephemeral poll tokens issued to remote monitor processes. Shorter limits exposure if a background process leaks its bearer.
Ceiling of events rendered by shared_md_render (the workspace Markdown digest).
Maximum size (UTF-8 bytes) of inline content in messages and artifacts before artifact_put is required.
'open': session credentials optional but validated when supplied. 'strict': sensitive verbs (message_create, handoff_*, inbox_*) require session_id + session_secret.
Window (days) for the event log: prune removes events older than this.
Window (days) for READ deliveries. The unread/delivered/parked lanes are never pruned.
Window (days) for CLOSED sessions. Active/stale sessions are never pruned.
Window (days) for MESSAGES: prune removes messages older than this by PURE AGE, regardless of delivery status, taking their deliveries and embeddings with them. Hard minimum 7 (fail-closed).

Semantic search over message content: 'off' disables it (no embeddings; /messages/search answers EMBEDDINGS_UNAVAILABLE); 'stub' uses a zero-dependency deterministic provider; 'local' uses sentence-transformers (requires the [embeddings] extra). Takes effect after a restart.
Anonymous usage metrics: 'disabled' writes nothing, 'local_only' keeps a local JSONL audit trail, and 'anonymous_beacon' publishes bounded aggregate deltas to the configured beacon.
Background publish cadence (s) for anonymous metrics. Changing this while serve is running takes effect after restart; the manual publish endpoint is available immediately.
Run the retention prune automatically on every server boot.
Deliver a read receipt to the sender's inbox when a recipient acknowledges its message (receipts never generate receipts). Turn off to keep inboxes receipt-free.

How read receipts appear in Meta-harness: 'inline' hides receipt notification turns and shows an aggregate acknowledgement flag on the original message; 'timeline' keeps receipts as separate chat turns.
Show each workspace's absolute project path (root_realpath) on the Workspaces screen and the /api/v1/workspaces API. Off (default) redacts the path (defense-in-depth); turn on to reveal it.
Show the operator attention projection of existing Nexus facts. Disabling it preserves Approvals, Handoffs and their original actions.
Seconds before an eligible open handoff without a claimant needs attention. 0 disables this time threshold; handoff leases and execution remain unchanged.
Seconds before an executor disconnected with pending work is escalated in attention. 0 disables this escalation; connection recovery and execution remain unchanged.
Opt-in: trace-id propagation across messages and handoffs so multi-agent trajectories can be reconstructed.
Opt-in: human-in-the-loop steering - operator pause, inject and redirect over agent coordination.
Opt-in: handoff verification - completion evidence is checked before a handoff closes.
Opt-in: handoff dependency graphs (depends_on) with dependency-aware claiming.
Experimental opt-in: shared memory primitives (memory_*) and the dashboard Memory tab. MCP tool exposure is decided at server startup.
Opt-in: coordination health reporting (windowed metrics over bus activity).
Runtime connections, enabled by default. Admission is checked on every request; MCP publication requires restart.
Opt-in: replay/eval export of coordination history (NDJSON + manifest).
